function: Learned 3D positions and excitation current weights of 16 UAVs forming a virtual antenna array for collaborative beamforming, maximizing rate and minimizing energy (p. 6-7).
system: 16 single-antenna rotary-wing UAVs forming a virtual array, 100 m x 100 m area, altitude 100-120 m, air-to-ground link to remote BSs, 2.4 GHz (p. 3, 12).
method: HATRPO-UCB: multi-agent trust-region policy optimization, fully connected actor-critic per UAV, Beta-distribution policy; reinforcement learning, trained offline on a central server (p. 8-10, 12).
data_channel: Own simulator built from the system model: probabilistic LoS air-to-ground channel [32], path loss exponent 2, 2.4 GHz; no dataset or measurement (p. 4, 12).
test_conditions: Training: 4x10^5 single-slot episodes, 16 UAVs, BS may differ across episodes. Testing: continuous service to two BSs; no unseen scenario stated (p. 9, 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: linear antenna array LAA, rectangular antenna array RAA. Learned: MADDPG, IPPO, MAPPO, conventional HATRPO (p. 12-13, Table III).
metrics: Transmission rate (bps), total UAV motion energy (J), average episode reward, convergence epochs, critic loss, rate under phase errors (p. 12-15).
complexity: Big-O of training and inference, e.g. inference O(n_uav times sum of layer products); no runtime or parameter count (p. 10-11).
openness: none; supplementary material cited only for Appendix A (reward tuning) and B (flight paths) (p. 1, 12-13).
q1_support: p. 12: "we build a simulation environment for the DRL model to interact and collect data"; the channel follows a probabilistic LoS model [32] (p. 4), and no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 13: "the actual performance of UVAA communicating continuously with two BSs"; the paper never says these BSs or the 16-UAV setting differ from training, where the BS may change per episode (p. 9).
q3_support: p. 2: "two classic antenna array solutions, three baseline MADRL algorithms and the conventional HATRPO"; p. 13: "Table III shows the numerical optimization results of various methods" (rate and energy).
q4_support: p. 11: "the computational complexity of HATRPO-UCB in the implementation stage is O(nuav"; training complexity is also given in Big-O on p. 10-11.
q5_support: p. 1: "supplementary downloadable material available at https://doi.org/10.1109/TMC.2024.3419915"; p. 12: "the tuning process and results are shown in Appendix A of the supplemental material", so it holds appendices, no code or dataset is stated.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3 by the tie-break order: beam control of an aerial link by a UAV virtual antenna array. The learned action sets UAV positions and excitation weights (p. 7), so it passes above_phy under the aerial-link rule. The supplementary file is not in the PDF; reviewer to confirm it holds no code or data (q5). Training BS distribution and test BS positions are not given (q2).
